TrailSource.description:
Which record a hop came from.

Kept on every hop because the trail's whole claim is that it agrees with what ran. A reader who
cannot tell which system said a thing cannot check it, and a trail nobody can check is a
narrative rather than a record.
TrailSource.title: TrailSource

TrailLink.description:
Where a hop can be followed to.

A hop carries a link or it carries none; it never carries a dead one. ``external`` distinguishes
leaving the studio (the VM diff, the running preview, the outbox) from staying inside it — the
design renders those as ``↗`` and ``→`` respectively, and a founder learns that distinction in one
screen.

external.description: True when following this leaves the studio.
external.title: External

href.description: An absolute URL, or a studio-relative path beginning with ``/``.
href.title: Href

label.description: What the link says. In the founder's language, never a URL.
label.title: Label

TrailLink.title: TrailLink

TrailHop.description:
One thing that happened to a ticket.

``verified`` is deliberately three-valued. ``true`` and ``false`` mean the signature was checked
and the answer is known; **absent** means verification does not apply to this kind of hop — a
commit is not signed by the approval secret and never was. Collapsing absent into ``false`` would
mark every commit as suspicious, which is how a warning stops being read.

at.description: When it happened, ISO-8601. The trail is ordered by this and by nothing else.
at.title: At

link.description: Where to follow it, when there is somewhere real to go.

text.description: What happened, in a founder's language. A sentence, not a status word.
text.title: Text

verified.description: Whether this hop's signature verified. Null when signing does not apply to its source.

TrailHop.title: TrailHop

description:
Everything that happened to one ticket, in order, joined from the records that already exist
(fountainbridge FB-125, gap G1).

The events are not new. ActiveGraph approvals, lane run reports, the repository's commits and
checks, and the venture box's preview all record their own part already — and none of them can be
reached by the founder whose work it is. This joins them so a ticket can be followed from the
founder's own words to something running.

Its claim, and the standard it is held to: *nothing shown here can disagree with what ran*. So a
trail never invents a hop, never renders a link it cannot resolve, and says when a source could not
be read rather than quietly returning a shorter story.

degraded.description:
True when a source could not be read. The trail is then incomplete and must say so — a
short trail and an unreadable one look identical otherwise, and one of them is a lie.
degraded.title: Degraded

hops.description:
Every hop, oldest first. May legitimately hold exactly one: a ticket filed and not yet
picked up has a real, complete, one-entry history.
hops.title: Hops

repo.description:
The venture repository the ticket lives in. Two repos in one venture may share an id
namespace, so a trail is only identified by both.
repo.title: Repo

ticket_id.description: The ticket this is the history of, e.g. ``ARCA-068``.
ticket_id.title: Ticket Id

title: Trail
